courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Literature Survey in CMB and Scientific Communication
courses.description: This pre-capstone course uses a ‘writing-to-learn’ approach that guides student step-by-step through the making of a primary research article in the life science discipline. The course introduces students to the process of problem solving in science through the scientific method of inquiry. The underlying principles of commonly used life-science methodologies for conducting research will be introduced through lectures while practical training in literature survey, information gathering, and data analysis will be provided through hands-on experience. The course will also introduce techniques in scientific communications by guiding students through each stage of the writing process and by conducting oral presentations, group discussion and peer reviews.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing the course, students are expected to be able to:

1. Perform literature search independently using online databases to find the relevant scientific information on a given topic

2. Understand the overall process of the scientific method of inquiry and apply it to identify and analyze scientific problems

3. Develop scientific writing and oral presentation skills including crafting arguments and supporting claims with the relevant evidence

4. Develop problem-solving skills and logical reasoning through critical evaluation of available data

5. Understand and appreciate the process of research discoveries, and the importance of information sharing in life science research

6. Develop effective communication skill and inter-personal skills through team work

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Research Internship
courses.description: The course provides the opportunity for students to earn University Credits (2 units) from one summer research internship in an academic or industrial setting. During the internship, students should be undertaking a CMB-related research project in an established laboratory with a time commitment of at least 160 hours. Internship work can be arranged either within or outside the university (can be overseas too).
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students should be able to:

* Apply knowledge and practical skills in CMB research
* Work independently on a research project in a laboratory setting under supervision
* Demonstrate essential data analytical skills and problem-solving abilities
* Develop proficiencies in scientific writings and oral presentations
* Demonstrate proper work attitude and research conduct

學生可在課程中獲得:

* 學習及應用細胞及分子生物相關的技術
* 在導師帶領下的獨立科學研究機會
* 展示基本的數據分析技能和解決問題的能力
* 培養科學寫作和口頭報告的能力
* 展示正確的工作態度和研究行為

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Cell and Molecular Biology Laboratory I
courses.description:
This laboratory course provides the practical experience in techniques of molecular biology and cell culturing. Project-based experimental projects are designed to guide students through the investigative process of scientific research. Molecular biology work includes the construction of the recombinant DNA clones tagged with fluorescent proteins (FPs) as well as the generation, characterization and purification of the encoded FP-tagged fusion proteins. In addition, the training in aseptic cell culturing techniques to handle E. coli, plant and mammalian cell lines is provided for the skill preparation of the subsequent transient expression, establishment of transgenic plants and cell lines carrying the previously constructed recombinant DNA clones.
Students’ progress will be evaluated through records of data analysis and evaluation in experimental logbooks, laboratory write-up and a final lab report in addition to quizzes and exams at term’s end. Students will also be divided into groups to produce a science video illustrating a Cell and Molecular Biology related topic of their own interests. Students are expected to demonstrate team-spirit through division of labor in the project as well as to learn and communicate science through self-motivated pursuit of knowledge.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this lab course series, students are expected to:

1. Demonstrate mastery of the scientific method, the design and application of the experiments and interpretation of the results to address questions related to CMB

2. Be proficient in basic laboratory skills in cell and molecular biology such as recombinant DNA techniques, plant and animal cell culturing techniques as well as bright-field and fluorescent microscopy techniques

3. Be able to synthesize ideas and generate hypothesis by reading and integrating scientific primary literature

4. Be proficient in scientific communication skills (written and oral) and the planning and organization of experimental projects

5. Develop a proper attitude towards science that values curiosity, creativity and innovation

6. Understand the importance of scientific integrity and ethical scientific conduct

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Cell and Molecular Biology Laboratory II
courses.description: This laboratory course is a continuation of CMBI3010 Cell and Molecular Biology Laboratory I. This laboratory course provides practical experience in the studies of cell biology. Project-based experimental projects are designed to guide students through the investigative process of scientific research. Different from traditional lab courses, which consist of separate and unrelated exercises, this CMB lab course is offered as term-long projects with all techniques or experimental methods incorporated into each project. Students will therefore not only learn various modern techniques, but also how and when these techniques are applied in life science research. In addition to the transgenic plant cell lines established in CMBI3010, this course will introduce students to transient expressions in animal cell models. Cell imaging approach employing high-end methodologies in microscopy to detect the expression and sub-cellular localization of fluorescent proteins as well as organelle dynamics will be used. Hands-on experience on conventional experimental methods including protein purification, Western blotting analysis and other common in-vivo or in-vitro cellular assays will also be provided.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this lab course series, students are expected to:

1. Demonstrate mastery of the scientific method, the design and application of the experiments and interpretation of the results to address questions related to CMB

2. Be proficient in basic laboratory skills in cell and molecular biology such as recombinant DNA techniques, plant and animal cell culturing techniques as well as bright-field and fluorescent microscopy techniques

3. Be able to synthesize ideas and generate hypothesis by reading and integrating scientific primary literature

4. Be proficient in scientific communication skills (written and oral) and the planning and organization of experimental projects

5. Develop a proper attitude towards science that values curiosity, creativity and innovation

6. Understand the importance of scientific integrity and ethical scientific conduct

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Cell and Molecular Biology Laboratory III
courses.description: This laboratory course provides the hands-on experience in various advanced microscopies that are commonly employed in cell biology research. Students first get familiar with the operation of the high-end microscopes in the laboratory. Subsequently, using the microscopes, students validate the materials established in CMBI3010, which will be used in CMBI3020 and CMBI3040.
courses.learning_outcomes:
The students taking this course are expected to achieve the following:

1. To learn the basic techniques in microscopy

2. To understand the principles of techniques in microscopy

3. To know how to apply these techniques in future experiments to solve practical problems

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Cell and Molecular Biology Laboratory IV
courses.description: This laboratory course provides the hands-on experience in the advanced techniques in cell and molecular biology research. The techniques include reporter gene assay, co-immunoprecipitation, real time polymerase chain reaction, and Forster resonance energy transfer. With the materials established and knowledge gained in CMBI3010, 3020 and 3030, students make use of these advanced techniques to explore new aspects in cell and molecular biology research.
courses.learning_outcomes:
The students taking this course are expected to achieve the following:

1. To learn the advanced techniques in cell and molecular biology

2. To understand the principles of these advanced techniques in cell and molecular biology

3. To know how to apply these techniques in future experiments to solve practical problems

courses.description: This course provides an overview on the phylogeny and basic biology of selected top model organisms including mouse, zebrafish, fruit-fly, Caenorhabditis elegans, Arabidopsis thaliana, and yeast. Due to their biological and technical advantages, these model organisms have been extensively employed for discovering a series of fundamental biological questions in the research of the modern life sciences. The course is instructed by our faculty members and invited speakers from other universities who use these models extensively in their researches.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students taking this course are expected to achieve the following:

1) To develop a sense of biodiversity

2) To understand phylogenetic relations of major groups of organisms

3) To understand the major advantages offered by various model organisms and the major fields of their uses

4) To be aware of various cutting-the-edge biotechniques that can be applied to these model organisms

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Protein Trafficking
courses.description:
This course covers the general principles of and current developments in protein trafficking for both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Specific topics include the structures and functions of transport vesicles, receptor-mediated protein transport, protein compartmentation in the secretory and endocytic pathways as well as in other organelles, protein degradation and the biological consequences of protein mis-localization in organisms. Students are required to watch online Lecture Videos in KEEP or Blackboard about Basic Knowledge in protein trafficking prior to the Lectures. These online Lecture Videos are supplemented with online quizzes in which students need to finish after watching these videos. In addition, students will also watch videos discussing recent Research Papers. During lectures, students will have in-depth discussion regarding the questions, key concepts and up-to-date research. By these means students will be able to clarify their concepts and be familiar with the latest research findings that are related to protein trafficking. Students will also learn the current developments of protein trafficking in details by delivering a presentation on a relevant topic derived from a recent research paper, with a Q&A session. The presentation will be graded by both Professor and peer students.

Blended-mode class section is available for this course. Please refer to the “Class Notes” of the blended-mode class section for details.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students taking this course are expected to achieve the following:

1) To understand the molecular mechanism of vesicular transport
2) To appreciate the rapid and current development in cellular trafficking
3) To acquire and appreciate the most up-to-date cellular technology and research methods
4) To synthesize new ideas from their knowledge on protein trafficking in research

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Protein Folding
courses.description: This course covers the energetics of protein folding including hydrophobic effect, hydrogen bond, electrostatic interactions, and conformational entropy, and how these factors interplay in protein folding and functions. Through detailed in-class discussion on the classic and the latest research literatures, students will learn how important theories and hypotheses of protein folding energetics were formulated, supported or disproved by experiments. The students will also learn how to apply the theories to improve protein stability in protein design and engineering through a group project.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students are expected to achieve the following:

1) To understand the energetics of protein folding, including hydrophobic effect, hydrogen bond, electrostatic interactions, and

conformational entropy

2) To understand how these energetic factors affect protein stability

3) To apply their knowledge learned in the design/engineering of proteins with improved protein stability

4) To synthesize new ideas from their knowledge on protein folding in research

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Signal Transduction
courses.description: This course covers the general principles, concepts and moderntechnologies in signal transduction for both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Specific topics include signal perception by different receptors, phosphorylation-mediated signaling, signaling crosstalk, and methodologies in signal transduction research.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students are expected to achieve the following:

1) To understand the basic and current development in signal transduction

2) To understand the current knowledge about the mechanisms and roles of signal transduction in controlling various biological functions

3) To appreciate the current literatures in signalling and biological function

William M W Mong Eng Bldg 712

courses.description: This advanced cell biology course provides a comprehensive review on current issues on cancer cell biology such as the molecular mechanisms of cancer pathogenesis, cancer cell proliferation and differentiation, programmed cell death (apoptosis), cell migration (metastasis), and the current technologies for cancer diagnosis and therapy.

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Stem Cell Biology

meetings.location: William M W Mong Eng Bldg 712
William M W Mong Eng Bldg 712

courses.description: This advanced cell biology course introduces basic cellular and molecular features of pluripotent stem cells and provides a comprehensive review on current important issues in stem cell research and regenerative medicine.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students taking this course are expected to achieve the following:

1) To understand basic cell and molecular biology of stem cells

2) To gain an insight into the potential applications of stem cell technology in regenerative medicine

3) To comprehend the literature and follow the most recent developments in the field of stem cell technology

4) To understand the current technologies used in stem cell research

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Neuronal Cell Biology

meetings.location: William M W Mong Eng Bldg 712

courses.description: This advanced cell biology course focuses on the basic functional units and development of the mammalian nervous systems. Special cellular and molecular features of neurons are also discussed. Other topics include neuronal polarity, membrane trafficking, axonal transport, axon guidance, synapse formation and synaptic plasticity.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students taking this course are expected to achieve the following:

1) To gain a deep knowledge of the unique features of neurons at cell and molecular levels

2) To comprehend the literature and follow the most recent developments in the field of neurobiology

3) To be aware of the current central issues in neuronal cell biology and neuroscience in general

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Genomics and Transcriptomics
courses.description: This advanced molecular biology course introduces the latest research focuses on genomics and transcriptomics. It covers the sequencing and mapping of the entire genome, methodologies in RNA gene expression profiling, structure and function of genes as well as regulation and dynamics of the transcriptome in an organism.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students taking this course are expected to achieve the following:

1) To understand principles and current status of genomics and transcriptomics

2) To gain basic knowledge of bioinformatics and instrumentations for data acquisition and analysis in genomics and transcriptomics

3) To comprehend the literature and follow the most recent developments in the field of genomics and transcriptomics

4) To be prepared for further research in genomics and transcriptomics

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Proteomics
courses.description: This advanced molecular biology course introduces the principles and methods of proteomics, the high-throughput investigation of proteins. In particular, the structural and functional relationships between proteins are discussed. The course provides students a global view of protein components involved in important biological pathways of living cells. Common web-based tools for protein sequence annotation, protein structure prediction and protein structure analysis are covered. Besides, advances in methodologies for discussion include the two-dimensional gel electrophoresis (2DE), liquid chromatography (LC), mass spectrometry and high throughput x-ray crystallography.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students taking this course are expected to achieve the following:

1) To understand principles and current status of proteomics

2) To comprehend the literature and follow the recent developments in the field of proteomics

3) To be prepared for future research in proteomics

courses.subject: CMBI
courses.title: Metabolomics
courses.description: This advanced molecular biology course aims to familiarize students with the latest research focuses in metabolomics, which concerns data acquisition and quantitative characterization of metabolites and metabolic pathways in living organisms. Modern technologies in profiling and identifying metabolites are introduced, and recent applications of metabolomics in various aspects of biology are also discussed.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students taking this course are expected to achieve the following:

1) To understand principles and current status of metabolomics

2) To gain basic knowledge of bioinformatics and its application in metabolomics

3) To comprehend the literature and follow the most recent developments in the field of metabolomics

4) To be prepared for further research in metabolomics

2) To appreciate the new and rapid development in cell biology research

3) To be able to propose future direction in research and development of cell biology

courses.learning_outcomes:
Students are expected to achieve the following:

2) To appreciate new development in molecular biology and propose future research

courses.subject: CMBI

William M W Mong Eng Bldg 804

courses.learning_outcomes:
Students are expected to achieve the following:

2) To understand the principles, development and application of these new biotechniques

3) To be able to propose future application and development of technology for research in cell and molecular biology
